open_errors.issue: Ch 5 says Asha 'had come to the fort at nineteen', and ch 12 speaks of 'her first month at the fort'. But Janu raised Devan and Asha at Kettamala. As a girl Asha drew parrots on the cistern-house walls (ch 12). She played seven wells there at four (ch 18). She once held her warden father's seal (ch 29). She grew up in the fort, so at nineteen she took up her post rather than arrived.
open_errors.fix: Make nineteen the age she took her officer's post at the fort, not the age she came to it.

patches.find: She had come to the fort at nineteen, and in her first month she had gone through the recruits with a slate and a bit of chalk, writing down names and villages and mothers.
patches.replace: She had taken her post as an officer of the fort at nineteen, and in her first month she had gone through the recruits with a slate and a bit of chalk, writing down names and villages and mothers.

patches.find: Her first month at the fort she had written the name of every recruit on it, with his mother's village beside, because she said a man fights harder for a captain who knows where his mother lives.
patches.replace: Her first month as an officer of the fort she had written the name of every recruit on it, with his mother's village beside, because she said a man fights harder for a captain who knows where his mother lives.

open_errors.issue: In ch 6 Devan slides his knife under the queen's green wax and 'the whole seal came away in one piece, the bird still crisp on its face'. In ch 32 the gift seal is described as one somebody 'cut in half to open a gift'.
open_errors.fix: Describe the gift seal as prised off its cord, not cut in half.

patches.find: The one on the writ was fuller and brighter, because nobody had cut that one in half to open a gift.
patches.replace: The one on the writ was fuller and brighter, because nobody had prised that one off a knot of cord to open a gift.

open_errors.issue: Ammu's Valli cover is 'a coast girl's blue cotton' in ch 18 and 'her blue cotton' in ch 20. In ch 26 it becomes 'the plain brown cloth of Valli', and in ch 28 'a small brown bundle'.

patches.find: She was mud to the knees, in the plain brown cloth of Valli the pepper trader's girl, her braid half down.
patches.replace: She was mud to the knees, in the plain blue cotton of Valli the pepper trader's girl, her braid half down.

patches.find: At the foot of the tree, in the roots, lay a small brown bundle: the cloth Ammu wore as Valli, the pepper trader's girl.
patches.replace: At the foot of the tree, in the roots, lay a small blue bundle: the cloth Ammu wore as Valli, the pepper trader's girl.

open_errors.issue: Ch 5 says Devan 'had seen these scars by lamplight on the wedding night'. But he pinched out the lamp before she turned (ch 1 and ch 2), and he watched her by starlight and in the dawn grey. He also saw the wrist scar on the rampart at sunset (ch 1), which makes 'not seen them in sun' too absolute.
open_errors.fix: Change lamplight to starlight and the dawn grey, and contrast it with full sun.

patches.find: He had seen these scars by lamplight on the wedding night. He had not seen them in sun.
patches.replace: He had seen these scars by starlight on the wedding night, and in the grey of the dawn after. He had not seen them in full sun.

open_errors.issue: On the wedding day Neela already thinks of Devan as 'A man who drilled alone at dawn.' Later chapters treat this as news. Janu tells her in ch 3 ('Every day before light'), and Neela files it as worth knowing. Ch 6 says she knew his early rising 'only from Janu's grumbling and from the pit lamps'. Ch 11 says rising was something she had 'only ever heard of, from Janu and from the lamps'.
open_errors.fix: Replace the ch 1 tally item with something she knows from the guild's drawings.

patches.find: So: forty days. A man who drilled alone at dawn. A fort with one great gate and sixty-odd soldiers.
patches.replace: So: forty days. A man in a high west room. A fort with one great gate and sixty-odd soldiers.
